name: KY-054 phototransistor
identification: Small black PCB with 3 angled header pins at one end and a dark blue round cap on two legs, sticking out past the board edge.

middle.say: middle pin, the one between S and minus

confirmations.question: Look at the 3 pins of the phototransistor. Is one marked S and one marked with a minus, with the third pin between them?
confirmations.reason: The pin order differs between modules. The wiring plan is only valid if S and minus are the outer pins and the supply pin is the one in the middle.

facts.statement: The module has three pins: signal (printed S), supply (+V, the middle pin) and ground (printed -). The vendor's drawing shows them in the order S, supply, -. Go by the printed markings.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-054, pin drawing (vendor documentation for the Joy-IT module; clones may differ)

facts.statement: The vendor's technical data gives an operating voltage of 3.3 V to 5 V.

A phototransistor and a fixed 10 kilohm resistor form a voltage divider between supply and ground; the signal pin carries the divided voltage, which changes with brightness. Powered from 3.3 V the signal cannot rise above 3.3 V.
facts.source: Joy-IT SensorKit, KY-054, description and code example
